$comment: Machine-readable address catalog for Extra Utilities G1 (BZR 2.2.301).
$comment2: Each entry carries the known hardcoded address alongside a 'pattern' field.
$comment3: Patterns are IDA-style byte sequences (?? = wildcard byte). Where no pattern has
$comment3b: been derived the field is null and a 'note' says why.
$comment3c: pattern_kind 'code': the pattern starts at 'address' (functions, hook and patch sites). pattern_kind 'reference': the pattern is a unique instruction sequence elsewhere that contains the address bytes (data globals, vftables, strings); 'note' names the matching instruction.
$comment4: Verify with: python tools/qualify_bzr_build.py <exe> --catalog. tools/validate_hardening.py fails when src/ uses an engine-range literal that is not catalogued here.
$comment4b: Derive new signatures from the GOG executable; the Steam executable is SteamStub-packed.

target.note: BZR is a 32-bit process. All absolute addresses are virtual addresses in the default load image.

dummynode.description: The executable's Lua 5.1 dummynode_. EXU links its own Lua core against the game's lua_State, and Lua5.1-BZR/src/ltable.c hard-codes this address as dummynode so both cores agree on the empty-table sentinel. If it moves, EXU's luaH_resize frees the host's static node (heap corruption).

setnodevector.description: Lua 5.1 setnodevector; the size==0 branch stores t->node = dummynode. Required runtime anchor: its signature embeds the dummynode address, so a build where the address moved fails before EXU creates any table.
setnodevector.note: Unique in GOG 2.2.301 .text (verified 2026-09-27). The executable has 7 imm32 references to dummynode, all in the Lua core.
